note_claims.claim: Head injury occurred after a mechanical fall at home at about 07:45.
The patient tripped on a rug and struck the left side of her head on a door frame.
The daughter reports the patient seemed muddled for about 10 minutes afterwards, though the patient has no memory of this.
Loss of consciousness is uncertain (unwitnessed).
There was one episode of vomiting in the car.
The patient experienced a mild headache at the impact site.
There was no visual disturbance, limb weakness, or neck pain.
There was no preceding dizziness or presyncope.
The last apixaban dose was taken this morning, after the fall.
Tetanus status is up to date.
The patient is on Apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily for atrial fibrillation.
The patient is on Bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily.
The patient is on Amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
The patient is allergic to penicillin, which causes swelling.
The Glasgow Coma Score (GCS) is 15.
There is a 3 cm laceration with a haematoma over the left temple.
Pupils are equal and reactive to light.
Strength is normal everywhere (normal power in all limbs).
There is no cervical spine midline tenderness.
Heart rate is irregular at about 80.
Blood pressure is 146 over 82.
A CT scan of the head is required due to the patient being on a blood thinner.
The evening's dose of apixaban will be withheld until the CT scan is reviewed.
The wound will be cleaned and closed with steri-strips.
Discharge is planned if the CT scan is normal, with the daughter staying with the patient for 24 hours.
The patient should call 999 or return immediately if she becomes drowsy, confused, vomits again, has a worsening headache, a fit, or any weakness.
Written head injury advice was given to the daughter.

transcript_facts.fact: The patient reported tripping on a rug in the hall and banging her head on the door frame.
The patient reported the time of the fall was about half past nine.
The relative corrected the time of the fall, stating it was about quarter to eight, noting that the post hadn't come and the patient hadn't had breakfast.
The patient stated the injury was to the left side, by her eye.
The patient stated she did not think she had blacked out.
The relative reported that the patient was muddled for about ten minutes after the fall, asking what day it was.
The relative reported that the patient was sick once in the car on the way to the clinic.
The patient reported having a bit of a headache where she hit it.
The patient reported no problems with her vision, weakness in her arms or legs, or neck pain.
The patient stated she did not feel dizzy before the fall and caught her foot on the rug.
The relative stated the patient is on Apixaban 2.5 milligrams twice a day for her heart rhythm.
The relative stated the patient is on Bisoprolol 2.5 milligrams once a day.
The relative stated the patient is on Amlodipine 5 milligrams once a day.
The patient stated she is allergic to penicillin, which makes her swell up.
The clinician noted the patient's Glasgow Coma Score is 15.
The clinician noted there is a cut about 3 centimetres long with a bump around it on the left temple.
The clinician noted the patient's pupils are equal and react to light.
The clinician noted the patient's strength is normal everywhere.
The clinician noted the patient's heart rate is irregular at about 80.
The clinician noted the patient's blood pressure is 146 over 82.
The clinician planned to hold off the evening's dose of apixaban until the CT scan is reviewed.
The clinician planned to clean the cut and close it with steri-strips.
The clinician stated that if the scan is normal, the patient can go home with the daughter, who will stay with her for 24 hours.
The clinician provided safety-netting advice to call 999 or return immediately if the patient becomes drowsy, confused, vomits again, has a worsening headache, a fit, or any weakness.

findings.note_span: Head injury after a mechanical fall at home at about 07:45.
findings.transcript_evidence: Relative: Mum, it was before that. The post hadn't come and you hadn't had your breakfast. It was about quarter to eight.
findings.rationale: The time of the fall is inconsistent between the note (07:45) and the transcript (7:45), representing a minor temporal inaccuracy.
